column3: “Opponents” is rendered “enemies,” and “the children of the exile” as “the people of the exile.”
NASB follows the reading read aloud, “to Him”; the written text has “not.”
“Not for you and for us to build” is rendered “You have nothing in common with us in building.”
“Making slack the hands” is rendered “discouraged.”
“Purpose” is rendered “counsel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Translated Aramaic” is rendered “translated from Aramaic”; the Hebrew may mean “in Aramaic.”
From here to 6:18 the text is Aramaic. “Lord of command” is rendered “the commander.”
The list of peoples is rendered partly as titles (“the judges and the lesser governors”); one name is rendered “that is.” The meaning of several words is uncertain.
“Took into exile” is rendered “deported,” and “caused to dwell” as “settled.”
NASB supplies “To”; “your servant” is rendered “Your servants.”
“From beside you” is rendered “from you,” and “have finished” as “are finishing.”
“Kings it will injure” is rendered “it will damage the revenue of the kings”; the meaning of the Aramaic word is uncertain.
“We eat the salt of the palace” is rendered “we are in the service of the palace.”
NASB supplies “so that”; “a revolt they were making” is rendered “they have incited revolt.”
“Before this” is rendered “as a result.”
“The word” is rendered “an answer.”
“Made distinct” is rendered “translated”; it may mean “read clearly,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“Rising up” is rendered “has risen up,” and “done by it” as “perpetrated in it.”
“Having mastery over” is rendered “governing.”
NASB supplies “work.”
“Be cautious of negligence” is rendered “beware of being negligent.”
“With force and power” is rendered “by force of arms.”
Close to the Aramaic.
